A good but simple game where you live through the life of Henry Halfhead. 

I came into this game blind, I remember seeing it on my steam page a few months ago, thinking it would be the same type of experience as some other of these games ive played, like Katamari. But its a bit simpler in a good way. 

The gameplay is simple and straight to the point, you are henry and you can become any object (kinda like Mario Oddysey). With this power you go through his life stage by stage while solving simple puzzles or doing tasks. Overall it feels smooth, letting you usually automatically pick the one you were aiming for, movement is a bit slow, but luckily the levels arent that big. 

The visuals were what sold me on the game, and I do enjoy it during the game. Some levels were a bit more pale/bland due to the lack of walls and the void you live in being 1 color, but overall it was pretty to see! 

The music and voice over worked well together, sometimes I would be a bit too fast for the announcer which would force the camera stuck until he was done talking, but it happened twice so not that big of a deal. 

The story is about growing up, and learning to live with it. It sounds a bit deeper than it really is, but it is still a nice message that gets explained. 

Overall, my only real complaint would be the price point, 13 euro's is a bit on the pricey side considering I got all the content i could get in the 2.3 hours. I would recommend getting it, but maybe wait for a sale!

I just finished playing through Henry Halfhead on stream and came to immediately write this review. If you're looking for a charming, silly, and even emotional tale with a strong sense of humour, you will absolutely love this game! Reminiscent of games such as Katamari, Pikuniku, and to a T, Henry Halfhead doesn't overstay its welcome and pulls the player through a simple, yet well-told story about Henry, merely half a head, who must navigate the difficulties and challenges of growing up different from everyone around them. The game is completeable in only a few hours, but with 300 objects to possess and 30 Steam achievements to go for, you'll find plenty of stuff to do after the credits roll. The game has a keen attention to detail that I really appreciate, and I was pleasantly surprised how the narrator would react to the various optional things Henry can do.

A few minor issues could potentially drag down the experience for some; for instance, the camera occasionally has issues, and objects (including Henry themselves) can clip through environments, though these issues were often brief and never game-breaking. Subtitles didn't fully match the narration at times, and swapping between multiple objects that were clumped up together was rather slow and a bit tedious, even when using the precision swapping mechanic.

Henry Halfhead is a charming experience that doesn't waste the player's time, and delivers a competent, heart-warming narrative that it sets out to tell. While some minor issues plague the title, I wouldn't be surprised if they were patched out within a few weeks' time, and I will update this review if/when that happens. Well done to the team at Lululu Entertainment, and I'm looking forward to what they deliver next!
